title: Repair deployment authentication, indexing, audit recovery and TLS
body:
Codex probes used an expired imported OAuth document, repository indexing serialized model calls and could starve completed projects, dashboard certificate reuse depended on transient Docker addresses, and recovery epochs permanently reported historical audit failure.

This change uses the canonical refreshed Vault token with cross-process refresh locking; retains explicit credential/account precedence; reuses only identical verified embedding inputs; gives busy query embeddings a bounded time budget; processes repository documents in bounded pairs across projects; and only selects complete generations for transactional cutover. Dashboard certificate reuse checks stable configured identities while issuance retains automatic address coverage.

Historical audit verification now independently verifies a sealed restored archive and its checkpoint MACs. Missing, mutable, empty, damaged or unattested archives fail closed. Archive/key identity changes and SQLite sidecars invalidate cached results. The archive is bound to the validated recovery-epoch identifier, so a later recovery cannot reuse an earlier archive's green result. The active recovery epoch remains separate. On the appliance, all 876 missing original events were recovered from physical blocks marked unwritten in the pre-recovery filesystem snapshot, and full historical chain/MAC verification passed. Original damaged evidence is retained in a verified backup and snapshot; no existing event was rehashed or synthesized.

Validation: C audit suite in the deployment-image builder and locally; additional archive/key/cache/sidecar and epoch-change regressions; disposable PostgreSQL coverage for concurrency bounds, readiness starvation, stale content/model rejection and exact vector reuse; Go race detector against the PostgreSQL fixture. The deployed hotfix passes readiness, a real enrolled-client Codex completion and model probes after the planned host reboot. The API independently reports restored historical verification green, the active chain intact, and all three original native memories preserved. An isolated runtime fixture also passed private HTTP/MCP authorship admission, model-authored memory correction and persistence across the memory-owner restart. Operational backfill completion is recorded separately from the source regression results.

See docs/validation/deployment-repair-1.0.2-2026-10-17.md and docs/validation/deployment-audit-index-recovery-2026-10-17.md for scope and evidence. Automatic reviews remain enabled.
